## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 50* (titled *Capucapukāraka*, translated as "Chomping") is a monastic training rule governing dining etiquette within the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text lays down the precept against making chomping or smacking noises while eating food [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule and its accompanying case material has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this training rule is preserved across virtually all major Buddhist monastic traditions [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali Vinaya, it corresponds directly to Bhikkhu Pātimokkha Sekhiya 50, Bhikkhu Parivāra Sekhiya 50, and the counterpart rules for nuns in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha, and Bhikkhunī Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. Beyond the Theravāda canon, direct parallels appear in the Prātimokṣa sūtras and Vibhaṅgas of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, and Dharmaguptaka schools preserved in Sanskrit fragments, Chinese, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. The rule also closely resembles the subsequent sekhiya rule prohibiting slurping (*Surusurukāraka*, Sekhiya 51) across these traditions [SuttaCentral].

Computational analysis by DharmaNexus identifies 86 matching passages of internal text reuse across 30 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. These matches reflect heavily standardized legal and narrative formulae shared with adjacent dining etiquette rules in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga, showing the highest degrees of reuse with Sekhiya 49 (segments §0.1–1.9), Sekhiya 48 (§0.1–1.4), Sekhiya 19 (§0.1–1.4), and Sekhiya 44 (§0.1–1.7.1) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
